title: Acinic cell carcinoma of the parotid gland
presentation:
Presentation
The patient presents with a left facial mass lesion for work-up. The lesion is painless.
discussion:
Case Discussion
An acinic cell carcinoma of the left superficial and deep parotid gland is definitively confirmed on excision histology in this case.
Based on the lesion's MR imaging characteristics the broad differential in this case unfortunately still includes all the salivary gland neoplasms:
Warthin's tumor
pleomorphic adenoma
adenoid cystic carcinoma
mucoepidermoid carcinoma
acinic cell carcinoma
Over 80% of acinic cell carcinomas occur in the parotid gland.

viewers.text:
There is a well-marginated, bilobed, mixed, solid-cystic left intraparotid mass lesion within the superficial and deep lobes. The lesion has heterogeneous signal intensity on multiparametric MR imaging due to its mixed nature. The lesion has a regional mass effect, displacing the left parapharyngeal space anteromedially, the left lateral pterygoid muscle anteriorly (masticator space), and the carotid space (post styloid parapharyngeal space ) posteromedially with no encasement or infiltration. There is asymmetric compression of the left longus colli muscle and no infiltration. There is a widening of the stylomandibular tunnel. There is no calcification suspected. There is avid enhancement post-contrast administration.
The right parotid gland and bilateral submandibular glands are normal.
There are no suspicious cervical lymph nodes.

title: Acinic cell carcinoma of the parotid gland
presentation:
Presentation
A new palpable, mildly painful mass at the right mandibular angle, noticed two weeks ago. No pertinent past medical history.
discussion:
Case Discussion
The right superficial parotid mass in this case first came to the patient's attention when he began having trouble sleeping on the right side. The mass was mildly tender to palpation, but there were no paresthesias or other evidence of facial nerve injury.
Imaging with CT demonstrated the cystic and solid lesion above without lymphadenopathy, and the subsequent MRI showed a similar mass, but more clearly demonstrated enhancement in the solid components of the mass. The mass was then referred for FNA and core biopsy under ultrasound guidance. The ultrasound appearance of the cystic and solid mass is relatively nonspecific.
Pre-biopsy, the differential for the mass is still relatively wide and "tissue is the issue."  Possible etiologies include:
Warthin tumor
adenoid cystic carcinoma
pleomorphic adenoma
mucoepidermoid carcinoma
acinic cell carcinoma
During the FNA, the cytopathologist remarked that all the smears he was seeing "looked just like acinar cells." On the core biopsy, a diagnosis of acinic cell carcinoma was made, a rare diagnosis.
qa_pairs: What is the most common malignant tumour of the parotid gland?
Although Warthin tumor and pleomorphic adenoma are the most common tumors, the most common *malignant* tumor is mucoepidermoid carcinoma.

title: Pleomorphic adenoma: parotid gland
discussion:
Case Discussion
Fine needle aspiration biopsy was consistent with a pleomorphic adenoma. The diagnosis was confirmed in the parotidectomy specimen above. 
Pleomorphic adenoma accounts for 70% to 80% of all neoplasms of salivary glands and it involves the parotid gland in almost 80% of cases. It is usually well-circumscribed and has pushing borders. The gross appearance depends upon the relative proportion of epithelial elements and stromal component which may range from myxoid to cartilage. Tumors with a prominent cartilaginous matrix have bluish-gray opalescent appearance as seen in this case.
This case has been reproduced with permission from Dharam M. Ramnani, MD's collection at WebPathology.com. Additional images are here.

viewers.text:
Parotidectomy and histology images described individually. 
Gross Pathology
Pleomorphic adenomas arising in the parotid gland usually have a pink-tan rubbery surface, well-defined pushing margins, and translucent areas of cartilaginous differentiation (as seen in this image). A rim of uninvolved salivary gland parenchyma is present around the tumor in this superficial parotidectomy specimen.
H&E
Pleomorphic adenomas often have a biphasic appearance caused by admixture of epithelium and stroma. The epithelial component here is arranged in tubular and glandular structures. The stroma has myxochondroid appearance
Microscopically, the pleomorphic adenomas consist of three elements: epithelial cells, myoepithelial cells, and stroma. The epithelial cells commonly form tubular or glandular structures and are surrounded by myoepithelial cells. The background stroma may be myxoid, chondroid, hyalinized, or vascular
Pleomorphic adenomas arising in the parotid usually have a thick fibrous capsule as seen here. The normal parotid tissue is to the upper right of the capsule and the tumor is on the lower left. The capsule can be variable in thickness and may even be absent. Pleomorphic adenomas arising in the minor salivary glands are well-demarcated but usually not encapsulated

title: Brain abscess with dual rim sign
presentation:
Presentation
Sudden weakness on the right side of the body, fever.
discussion:
Case Discussion
Dual rim sign is seen on T2/FLAIR/SWI, comprising two concentric rims surrounding the abscess cavity, the outer one is hypointense, and the inner one is hyperintense. 
Dual rim sign helps distinguish an abscess from a glioblastoma. The hypointense rim typically demonstrates a thin, complete, regular overlapping the contrast-enhancing rim in cerebral abscesses. In glioblastoma, the T2 hypointense line is inner to the contrast-enhancing rim and is irregular, incomplete.
On histopathology, the outer rim corresponds to the capsule abscess in which the production of paramagnetic free radicals by macrophages resulting in magnetic susceptibility 1. The granulation tissues between the necrotic center and capsule are responsible for the hyperintense inner rim 1,2.
In contrast, the random deposition of hemorrhagic products at the edge of the necrotic cavity glioblastoma causes the irregular, incomplete, hypointense margin on SWI 1,2.

title: Tuberculous brain abscess
presentation:
Presentation
Headache for more than 3 months. Her symptoms began with projectile bouts of vomiting initially. An MRI scan was performed for further evaluation.
discussion:
Case Discussion
The presence of irregular wall thickening favors a malignant process, and lack of marked peripheral edema, also indicates a benign lesion. On the other hand, the location of this lesion, in the deep white matter, suggests the diagnosis of lymphoma. However, the patient underwent a craniotomy and the mass was resected. Histopathology revealed that no malignant cell was observed, and the diagnosis of malignancy was excluded, so the presence of brain abscess has been implicated and microbiology evaluation was performed. Although the abscess has generally a thin wall, in this case, we can see the opposite. Unfortunately, the microbiological test performed a few hours prior to the patient's death revealed that the causative organism was Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Because extensive peripheral edema is a hallmark finding of metastasis, GBM or abscess differential diagnosis of intracerebral space-occupying lesions with ring enhancement includes them.
Regarding this same patient, due to the partial treatment and use of corticosteroid, a thicker capsule and less amounts of edema were found, whilst the granulomatous abscesses tend to make a thicker ring on their own.

viewers.text: The MRI shows a well-defined thick-walled cystic lesion in the left basal ganglia which has mild peripheral edema and associated with considerable mass effect, especially on the foramen of Monro, which causes obliteration of the left frontal horn of the lateral ventricle. After the administration of contrast medium, the mass shows thick ring-like enhancement. You can see a small projection of the mass in the medial side of it, which seems to be trying to cross the midline and creates the butterfly fashion.

title: Glioblastoma - solitary ring enhancing lesion
presentation:
Presentation
Headache and seizures. No history of trauma, fever, neurological deficit, or weight loss.
discussion:
Case Discussion
Craniotomy and biopsy of the left frontal lobe tumor.
Histopathology: Glioblastoma (WHO grade IV). 
The tumor is very cellular comprising epithelioid and spindle cell sarcomatous components as well as striking giant cells often with bizarre features together with extensive necrosis. Immunohistochemistry shows a negative reaction to cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and strong reactivity of tumor and brain tissue to vimentin.  CD34 is also negative. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) shows focal immunoreactivity of viable as well as a necrotic tumor but the vast majority of the giant cells are nonreactive or only weakly reactive.

viewers.text:
FINDINGS: A space-occupying lesion with enhancing thick irregular walls and central necrotic core is seen in the left frontal lobe white matter. Marked surrounding vasogenic edema, effacement of the underlying ipsilateral lateral ventricle, and contralateral midline shift of 8 mm are noted. No other focal space-occupying lesion is seen.
CONCLUSION: Left frontal lobe ring-enhancing space-occupying lesion with mass effect, which is likely a primary brain tumor; other possible differential includes brain abscess & solitary brain metastasis.

title: Adrenal hematoma
presentation:
Presentation
During hemoptysis workup, a left retroperitoneal mass was incidentally found on imaging and further evaluated with multi-phase MRI abdomen. Of note, patient was on anticoagulation for cardiac dysrhythmia.
discussion:
Case Discussion
Given the small, enhancing nodule of indeterminate etiology, the patient underwent left adrenalectomy. Pathology showed a large adrenal hematoma with microscopic myelolipoma and negative for carcinoma.
A few take-home points for adrenal hematomas:
may be unilateral or bilateral
bilateral hemorrhage can cause adrenal insufficiency, which can lead to adrenal crisis and has the potential to be fatal 2
predisposing factors are numerous: anticoagulation use, infection, trauma, coagulopathic states 1
highly variable in size and internal complexity. The chronicity of blood products, from acute to chronic, have a specific appearance on T1 and T2, as the hemoglobin molecules break down 3
retractile blood clots can have an irregular appearance
utilize subtraction post-contrast sequences to negate the intrinsic T1 signal
enhancement in a large adrenal mass can indicate a secondary underlying etiology for the hemorrhage, such as adrenal myelolipoma, adrenal adenoma or adrenal carcinoma, or metastases
myelolipoma is a risk factor for hemorrhage, usually when they are larger
Case co-author: Fadi Moaikel, DO

viewers.text:
A complex, cystic mass in the retroperitoneum is centered at the left adrenal gland, which can be seen just medially to the mass, best on the axial T2 series. Note, there is NO claw sign with the kidney.
The mass is predominantly T2 hyperintense, which persists after fat saturation. Within the mass are strand-like and nodular areas of T2 hypointense signal, which, along the periphery, are intrinsically T1 hyperintense, suggestive of hemorrhagic components superimposed on the cystic components. Post-contrast, subtraction sequence shows previously T1 hyperintense signal on pre-contrast does not enhance.
There is an approximately 1 cm nodular focus of enhancement along the inferior-posterior aspect of the mass. No signal dropout was evident on opposed phase sequences (not shown).

title: Metastatic testicular germ cell tumor
presentation:
Presentation
Know and operated case of left testicular germ cell tumor. Post-chemotherapy follow-up CT.
discussion:
Case Discussion
This is a known and operated case of the left testicular germ cell tumor with pulmonary, hepatic, and retroperitoneal metastasis.
Cystic change is expected in germ cell tumors that respond to chemotherapy.

viewers.text:
Post-operative changes are seen in the left inguinal regions due to the left orchiectomy.
Several nodules less than 22 mm are seen at both lung fields, inferring metastasis.
A 175 × 90 × 115 mm well-defined mass with heterogeneous enhancement, internal cystic changes, and some foci of calcification is present at the left para-aortic regions. It partially encases the aorta and completely encases the inferior mesenteric artery. The left psoas muscle and the mid part of the left ureter are infiltrated by the mass, causing left-sided mild hydronephrosis and relatively renal parenchymal atrophy.
Multiple masses at the liver less than 50 mm show mild delayed peripheral enhancement, suggesting cystic metastasis.
A 5 mm stone is noted in the gallbladder.
